title: Earth Science Basics
description: Rocks, plate tectonics, weather and the layers of our planet

questions.question: What is the outermost solid layer of the Earth called?
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin rocky outer shell. Beneath it lie the mantle, the liquid outer core and the solid inner core.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when magma or lava cools and solidifies?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks such as granite and basalt form from cooled molten rock. Sedimentary rocks form from compacted sediment, and metamorphic rocks from rock changed by heat and pressure.

questions.question: What is the name of the theory that Earth's surface is divided into moving plates?
questions.explanation: Plate tectonics explains that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the mantle, causing earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building.

questions.question: What scale is commonly used today to report the size of large earthquakes?
questions.explanation: Seismologists use the moment magnitude scale for large earthquakes. The Beaufort scale measures wind, Mohs measures mineral hardness and Fujita rates tornadoes.

questions.question: Which mineral has a hardness of 10 on the Mohs scale?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural mineral and sits at 10. Corundum is 9, topaz 8 and quartz 7.

questions.question: In which layer of the atmosphere does almost all weather occur?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer, and it holds most of the atmosphere's mass and water vapor, so clouds and weather form there.

questions.question: What is the process by which water vapor turns into liquid water, forming clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when water vapor cools and changes to liquid droplets, which gather into clouds.

questions.question: What is the name of the supercontinent that existed about 300 to 200 million years ago?
questions.explanation: Pangaea joined nearly all landmasses before breaking apart. Gondwana and Laurasia were the two large pieces it split into.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and nearly 1% argon. Carbon dioxide is a small fraction of a percent.

questions.question: What do we call a crack in Earth's crust along which rocks have moved?
questions.explanation: A fault is a fracture where blocks of rock have slipped past one another. Sudden slip along a fault causes earthquakes.
